description: Choices under sustained use and proportional implementation effort, without timing slogans.

evals.name: design-for-sustained-session
evals.prompt: Choose an implementation for a browser work queue. A session starts with 20 items; users keep it open for days, add thousands of items, and receive frequent status updates. Option A synchronously serializes every item to localStorage on each update and takes 10 minutes to implement. Option B keeps current items in memory and asynchronously persists changed records with bounded retention and explicit failure handling; it takes 25 minutes. Give a concise recommendation and the main implementation boundaries. Do not run commands.
expectations: Chooses asynchronous changed-record persistence rather than synchronously rewriting the growing collection
Accounts for cumulative repeated work and retention under long sessions, rather than judging only the initial 20-item case
Keeps interaction usable on storage failure and addresses pending writes or interrupted persistence
Explains concrete consequences without announcing compliance with a time-awareness instruction or claiming agents are universally faster than humans

evals.name: proportional-complete-fix
evals.prompt: A settings dialog displays the wrong label because two call sites independently format the same enum. Both are identified. A shared existing formatter already handles every enum case. Reusing it in those two places and checking the affected cases takes 8 minutes. Hardcoding the currently reported label takes 3 minutes. A new extensible formatting framework takes several hours. What should you do? Answer in two sentences; do not run commands.
expectations: Chooses the existing shared formatter for both affected call sites and focused verification
Rejects the one-label patch without proposing the unnecessary new framework
Considers recurrence or maintenance consequences rather than treating shortest immediate implementation as sufficient
Does not announce internal time-awareness rules or make unsupported agent-versus-human speed claims
